title: 汉江临泛
author: 王维
intro: Boating on the Han River near Xiangyang, Wang Wei paints like a landscape artist: the river flows beyond heaven and earth, the hills appear and vanish in the haze, whole towns seem to float on the water.
analysis: 这是王维在襄阳一带泛舟汉江时写的山水诗，像一幅水墨画。开头两句写汉江的地理形势：它连着楚地的边塞和湖南的三湘，在荆门与长江的众多支流相通，一下子把视野拉得很宽。第二联最有名：江水好像流到了天地之外，远山在雾气中若有若无。这正是中国山水画的“留白”——远处画得淡淡的，看不清，反而显得更远、更大。第三联写船在波浪中起伏，看岸边的城镇好像漂浮在水上，远处的天空也在晃动，写得真实又有趣。最后说襄阳风景这么好，我愿意留下来，和“山翁”一起喝个痛快——山翁指晋代在襄阳爱喝酒的山简。
analysisEn: Wang Wei wrote this while boating on the Han River near Xiangyang, and it reads like an ink-wash landscape. The opening couplet sets out the geography in broad strokes: the river touches the old frontiers of Chu and the three Xiang rivers of Hunan, and at Jingmen it joins the nine branches of the Yangtze — a map that instantly makes the view enormous. The second couplet is the famous one: the river flows on beyond heaven and earth; the colours of the hills hover between there and not there. This is the poetic version of a key idea in Chinese painting, “leaving blank space” (留白): far-off things are painted faint and hazy, and that vagueness makes them feel farther and vaster. In the third couplet the boat rises and falls on the waves, so the towns on the shore seem to float, and even the distant sky seems to move — a real experience anyone who has been in a small boat will recognise. Finally he says Xiangyang’s wind and sunshine are so fine that he would like to stay and get drunk with the “old man of the mountain”, Shan Jian, a Jin-dynasty governor of Xiangyang famous for his love of wine.
background: Wang Wei (701–761) travelled south to Xiangyang around 740 on an official assignment. The poem is also titled “Gazing from the Han River” (汉江临眺) in some editions.
pronunciation: 郡邑 jùn yì。浦 pǔ。襄 xiāng。与 yǔ。荆门九派：派 pài（支流）。
version: 采用通行版本（与《全唐诗》一致）；题目有的版本作《汉江临眺》。异文：“好风日”一作“风日好”，“山翁”一作“山公”。

lines.lit: The frontiers of Chu connect with the Three Xiang;
lines.en: Here the old borders of Chu meet the Xiang rivers,

lines.lit: at Jingmen the nine branches flow through.
lines.en: and at Jingmen nine streams run into one.

lines.lit: The river flows beyond heaven and earth;
lines.en: The river flows on past the edge of the world;

lines.lit: the colour of the hills is between being and not being.
lines.en: the hills fade in and out of the haze.

lines.lit: Towns float on the shore ahead;
lines.en: Towns seem to float on the shore ahead;

lines.lit: the waves move the distant sky.
lines.en: the waves set the far sky rocking.

lines.lit: Xiangyang has fine wind and sun;
lines.en: Xiangyang’s breeze and sunlight are so fine,

lines.lit: I stay to get drunk with the Old Man of the Mountain.
lines.en: I’ll stay and drink with the old man of the hills.

words.note: 泛：坐船在水上漂，如“泛舟”。
楚：古国名，大致在今湖北、湖南一带。
今天“三湘大地”仍指湖南。
派：河流的支流。“九”表示多。

words.en: between being and not being; faintly visible

words.note: 郡、邑都是古代的地方行政单位。
今天多用于地名，如上海“浦东”。
现代汉语“波澜壮阔”，也比喻事情的起伏。

words.en: the Old Man of the Mountain (Shan Jian)
words.note: 指晋代镇守襄阳、爱喝酒的山简。

imagery.name: 江
imagery.zh: 汉江浩浩荡荡，好像流到天地之外，写出江面的辽阔。
imagery.en: The Han River seems to flow beyond the edge of the world, showing how vast it is.

imagery.name: 山
imagery.zh: 远山在雾气中若隐若现，像水墨画里淡淡的远景。
imagery.en: Distant hills fade in and out of the haze, like faint washes in an ink painting.

imagery.name: 天地
imagery.zh: “天地外”把视野推到极远，写出空间的无边无际。
imagery.en: “Beyond heaven and earth” pushes the view to the very limit, a sense of boundless space.

imagery.name: 酒
imagery.zh: 留在襄阳与“山翁”同醉，表达对这里风景的喜爱。
imagery.en: Staying to drink with the “old man of the hills” shows how much the poet loves this place.
